title: Convoy admission rate controller & attention-hint protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We observe a recurring tail-latency mode when the runtime mixes many small, bursty prefill requests with long-sequence decodes. Existing admittance heuristics admit per-request which creates many tiny kernel launches and poor kernel packing. Kernel selection also oscillates because attention characteristics (dense vs. sparse, short vs. long context) are not signaled until after prefill kernels are chosen.

Goal: Reduce 95/99th percentile latency for mixed workloads by: (1) grouping incoming requests into convoy windows that favor packability without increasing median latency for interactive traffic, (2) adding per-tenant soft shaping to protect long-lived decodes from starvation, and (3) propagating a lightweight attention-hint protocol so kernel selection can pick an appropriate optimized code path at prefill time.

Proposal summary: Implement a Convoy Admission Rate Controller (CARC) layered into the admission path. CARC will maintain short rolling windows (configurable, default 5-15ms) and create convoys of compatible requests according to a compact compatibility key (model, quantization profile, requested max-tokens, attention-hint). Compatibility checks prioritize packing gain vs. latency risk. Add per-tenant soft-shaping tokens so high-throughput tenants get minimal fair-share guarantees while preserving burst capacity for interactive tenants. Finally, define a 3-bit attention-hint in the request metadata: {0: unknown, 1: short-dense, 2: long-dense, 3: sparse/structured}. Runtime kernels will accept this hint to prefer specialized kernels earlier in the prefill pipeline.

Design details: Convoy windows are adaptive: start at 5ms and expand when estimated packing benefit improves. A lightweight estimator uses recent sequence-length distribution and current GPU occupancy to decide whether to expand. Packing algorithm favors slot-fill thresholds (e.g., >60% tokens filled) and avoids mixing requests with incompatible quantization. Per-tenant soft shaping uses a leaky-bucket with two tiers: guaranteed baseline throughput and burst credit. The shaping policy is configurable per-tenant via the console.

Attention-hint protocol: expose an optional header in the REST/SDK API (attention_hint: 0|1|2|3). SDKs will default to 0 (unknown) and provide heuristics (client-side heuristics: user-provided context_type, average prompt length, deterministic routing for embeddings) to emit hints. Server-side fallbacks will run a cheap sample-based attention fingerprint on the first micro-batch (sub-millisecond) if hint==0. Kernel selection mapping will be updated to consult the attention-hint before final kernel binding.

Telemetry and observability: Add metrics: convoy_window_ms, convoy_pack_ratio, convoy_padding_overhead, per_tenant_shaping_tokens, attention_hint_distribution, kernel_mismatch_rate (hint vs. actual), and downstream SLO buckets. Add a per-route dashboard and a synthetic workload harness to measure the 50/95/99 latencies under mixed burst/long-sequence patterns.

Safety and rollback: feature-flagged rollout (runtime flag + per-tenant console toggle). Default: CARC disabled for tenants with less than X requests/sec to avoid penalizing very low throughput customers. Gradual rollout: internal traffic -> opt-in beta tenants -> 10% wide -> 50% -> 100%. Automatic rollback on SLO regressions detected by the Optimize regression monitor.

Acceptance criteria: 1) 95th latency reduction >= 20% on mixed synthetic workload with <2% median change; 2) kernel_mismatch_rate < 3% after one hour of traffic; 3) no customer-facing errors introduced; 4) Console shows per-tenant shaping controls and telemetry.

Implementation plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement CARC admission layer and simple convoy windowing with conservative defaults; add telemetry. Phase 2 (2 weeks): implement per-tenant soft shaping and console controls; integrate with quota system. Phase 3 (2 weeks): implement attention-hint header plumbing and kernel selection hook; add SDK hinting guidance. Phase 4 (1 week): e2e testing, synthetic load validation, rollout to beta tenants.

Risks and trade-offs: Increasing convoy windows risks added latency for low-packing interactive requests. We mitigate via adaptive windows and per-tenant opt-out. Attention-hint may be misused; fallbacks and kernel mismatch telemetry reduce risk. Per-tenant shaping introduces quota complexity for billing and quotas; coordinate with billing and SRE.

Links: Design doc draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Convoy+Admission+Controller (draft). Synthetic harness results: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/convoy/mixed-workload (internal). Related PR (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2701
